I wanted to be more active in my community lately in an effort to try and impact change on a small scale, hoping that it would eventually spark a bigger change. Because of this I signed up for [Represent.Us](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5tu32CCA_Ig) and some other things to stay up to date on what's going on in America and what I can do to help. It seems however, that the information I gave them was shared with other organizations, which now send me constant mail about signing a petition to do so and so. I would be fine with this, except for the fact that each of these petitions require me to donate at least $5 to the cause in addition to my signature (I may be interpreting their letters wrong, but this is the impression I got). Due to this, along with knowledge that many charities only give a laughably small amount to the causes they are championing, I became quickly turned off as a part of me says many of these organizations are scams and even if they're not, I'd be wasting a whole lot of my own money for something that would institute little to no change.

Recently I received an email from EFF asking me to chip in $5 or more to stop Congress from banning encryption. I trust EFF, however I'm curious as to how me chipping in $5 is going to help. Now, I understand that it'll help with lawyer fees and whatnot, but is there anything else it will do? Furthermore, I used to receive a lot of emails from Rand Paul asking for donations; I'm assuming this is to finance his campaign to buy ads to promote himself more?

TL;DR:

How does my donating money to causes actually help these groups achieve their goals? Is there a more effective way to fight for what's important to me (stopping government from infringing on our rights mainly)? Yes I know someone is going to say it is time we use the 2nd Amendment, but I do not want to resort to violence as I know it will be a futile effort without organization. I would be arrested or killed, while said keyboard warrior there just foams at the mouth about taking our country back, but not doing anything themself.
How does a donation help a cause?

How does my donating money to causes actually help these groups achieve their goals?

It doesn't. however $5 x 10,000 people (or more) does. This world is run on money. Want people to fight for you rights, then you need to pay for people trained in this to do such. The lawyers gotta eat too. Not to mention server/site maintenance staff, journalists to cover and inform you what is going on, management staff, promotional staff, etc.

Is there a more effective way to fight for what's important to me (stopping government from infringing on our rights mainly)?

Get into politics and make a change. Start with local politics like zoning commission member, and work you way into a position which you can help change the laws. Yes this will take years to do, which is why we have career politicians. It will help you if you have a business going into politics. Probably going to have to devote your life to the cause.

Or you can give EFF $5. They decided to go the organization route and have been fairly successful. We know whats going on now, we have a voice to fight for us in court, and we have people who have devoted their lives to the cause so we can browse on Voat and look a cat pics.
